aboutMe.heading: About us
aboutMe.person1Bio: I’ve always loved logical thinking and algorithmic problem-solving, as it was my way of being creative. This creativity has remained with me throughout the years, and although I’m not great at typical “artsy” things, I find technology and programming truly captivating tools that enable me to create and fascinate me. When I strongly believe in something, I fervently dedicate myself to it and work day and night until it comes to life. For me, community is vital. Oh, and I love traveling!
aboutMe.person2Bio: Paulina Święcicka holds a leadership role at Roche as the Global Head of Data Management and Data Quality Platforms (previously serving as Head of Data Engineering, among other roles). She is responsible for driving enterprise data management, data quality, and AI-driven software innovations supporting R&D operations. Additionally, she is actively involved in digital transformation initiatives and empowering women in the technology sector.

ptpn.title: A talk at the National Conference of Neurological Nurses
ptpn.short: In October 2026, Dominika will talk about the ethical use of LLMs and patient data privacy.
full: At the National Conference of Neurological Nurses, Dominika will talk about the ethical and correct use of large language models (LLMs) in patient care.

The talk will focus on data privacy and security — what needs to be kept in mind before any patient information is passed to an AI tool. It's an important topic for a community that works closest with people living with MS every day.

gfr.title: We're organizing the finale of the HerStory project by Girls Future Ready
gfr.short: On July 31, 2026, we'll run a workshop for young women on technology in medicine at the finale of the HerStory program — using our project as an example.
full: At the finale of the Girls Future Ready foundation's HerStory program, we'll lead a workshop on technology in medicine — using our project as an example.

We'll focus on artificial intelligence: showing participants how to go from an idea to a working tool, and how to do it ethically. It's also a chance to tell the story of the mentoring that gave rise to this project.

hba.title: A talk at the "The Power of Mentoring" meeting by HBA
hba.short: Our project at the "The Power of Mentoring" meeting — on what comes out of combining mentoring, collaboration, and AI.
full: At the "The Power of Mentoring" meeting, organized by the Warsaw branch of the Healthcare Businesswomen's Association, Roche Polska, the Business Women Leaders Foundation, and Girls Future Ready joined forces.

We presented our project there as an example of what can emerge from the combination of collaboration, mentoring, and artificial intelligence. We showed how a mentoring relationship can give rise to a real tool that supports patients with multiple sclerosis.

smicoztego.title: We attended the "MS – so what?" conference
smicoztego.alt: photo from the SM - i co z tego? conference
smicoztego.short: We took part in the expert day and the patient days of the National Conference
full: Dominika took part in the expert day and the patient days of the National Conference "MS – so what?" — one of the largest events in Poland dedicated to multiple sclerosis.

It was an opportunity to hear firsthand which questions and problems truly concern patients — from diagnosis, through treatment, to everyday life with MS. The insights gathered fed into our question search tool and helped us better understand the community's needs.
